Hope was awarded more than 2,000 honors and awards, including 54 honorary university doctorates. In 1963 President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") awarded him the [Congressional Gold Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Gold_Medal "Congressional Gold Medal") for service to his country.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002152%E2%80%93153-110) President [Lyndon Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_Johnson "Lyndon Johnson") bestowed the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom "Presidential Medal of Freedom") in 1969 for his service to the armed forces through the [USO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USO "USO").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-usa-patriotism.com-111) In 1982 he received the S. Roger Horchow Award for Greatest Public Service by a Private Citizen, an honor given annually by [Jefferson Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Awards "Jefferson Awards").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Horchow_Award-112) He was presented with the [National Medal of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Medal_of_Arts "National Medal of Arts") in 1995[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-National_Medal_of_Arts-113) and received the [Ronald Reagan Freedom Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award "Ronald Reagan Freedom Award") in 1997.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Times_Union_1997-114) On June 10, 1980, he became the 64th—and only civilian—recipient of the United States Air Force [Order of the Sword](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Sword_(United_States) "Order of the Sword (United States)") which recognizes individuals who have made significant contributions to the enlisted corps.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Air_University-115)

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/Nancy_Reagan_presents_Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award_to_Bob_Hope.jpg/250px-Nancy_Reagan_presents_Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award_to_Bob_Hope.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nancy_Reagan_presents_Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award_to_Bob_Hope.jpg)

[Nancy Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") prepares to present Hope (then aged 94) with the [Ronald Reagan Freedom Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan_Freedom_Award "Ronald Reagan Freedom Award"), July 1997

Several buildings and facilities were renamed for Hope, including the historic [Fox California Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Theater_(Stockton,_California)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Fox Theater (Stockton, California) (page does not exist)") in downtown [Stockton, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockton,_California "Stockton, California"),[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Mohawk_Group-116) and the [Bob Hope Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope_Airport "Bob Hope Airport") in [Burbank, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Daily_News_2010-117) There is a Bob Hope Gallery at the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-118) In memory of his mother, Avis Townes Hope, Bob and Dolores Hope gave the [Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_the_National_Shrine_of_the_Immaculate_Conception "Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception") in Washington, D.C., a chapel called the Chapel of [Our Lady of Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Hope "Our Lady of Hope").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-119)[USNS _Bob Hope_(T-AKR-300)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Bob_Hope "MV Bob Hope") of the U.S. [Military Sealift Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Sealift_Command "Military Sealift Command") was named for the performer in 1997. It is one of very few [U.S. naval ships that were named after living people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._military_vessels_named_after_living_Americans "List of U.S. military vessels named after living Americans").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FAS_2011-120) The Air Force named a [C-17 Globemaster III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-17_Globemaster_III "C-17 Globemaster III") transport aircraft the _Spirit of Bob Hope_.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Warplanes_Online_Community-121)

In 1965, he was awarded an honorary Doctor of Humane Letters (L.H.D.) degree from [Whittier College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittier_College "Whittier College").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-122)

In 1978, Hope was invited to [dot the "i"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University_Marching_Band#Script_Ohio_and_dotting_the_%22i%22 "Ohio State University Marching Band") in the [Ohio State University Marching Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University_Marching_Band "Ohio State University Marching Band")'s "Script Ohio" formation, an honor only given to non-band members on 14 occasions from 1936 through 2016.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-123)[Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen") wrote and narrated a documentary honoring him, _My Favorite Comedian_, shown at [Lincoln Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln_Center "Lincoln Center").[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-124) In Hope's hometown of Cleveland, the refurbished [Lorain-Carnegie Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorain-Carnegie_Bridge "Lorain-Carnegie Bridge") was renamed the Hope Memorial Bridge in 1983, though differing claims have been made as to whether the bridge honors Hope himself, his entire family, or his stonemason father who helped in the bridge's construction. Also, East 14th Street near [Playhouse Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playhouse_Square "Playhouse Square") in Cleveland's theater district was renamed Memory Lane-Bob Hope Way in 2003 in honor of the entertainer's 100th birthday.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-125)

In 1992, Hope was honored with the "Lombardi Award of Excellence" from the Vince Lombardi Cancer Foundation. The award was created to honor the football coach's legacy, and is awarded annually to an individual who exemplifies his spirit. He was also inducted into [Omicron Delta Kappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omicron_Delta_Kappa "Omicron Delta Kappa"), the National Leadership Honor Society, in 1992 at [Ferris State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferris_State_University "Ferris State University"). On May 28, 2003, President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") established the [Bob Hope American Patriot Award](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Executive%20Order%2013306 "s:Executive Order 13306").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-126)

**Academy Awards** Although he was never nominated for a competitive Oscar, Hope was given five honorary awards by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences"):[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-awardsdatabase-127)

*   [25th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/25th_Academy_Awards "25th Academy Awards") (1952): Honorary Award for his contribution to the laughter of the world, his service to the motion picture industry, and his devotion to the American premise
*   [32nd Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32nd_Academy_Awards "32nd Academy Awards") (1959): [Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean_Hersholt_Humanitarian_Award "Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award")
*   [38th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/38th_Academy_Awards "38th Academy Awards") (1965): Honorary Award: first Academy Gold Medal for unique and distinguished service to the industry and the academy

### Marriage and relationships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Marriage and relationships")]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/1942-08-02_Residence_of_Bob_Hope%2C_North_Hollywood%2C_California_A.jpg/250px-1942-08-02_Residence_of_Bob_Hope%2C_North_Hollywood%2C_California_A.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1942-08-02_Residence_of_Bob_Hope,_North_Hollywood,_California_A.jpg)

Residence of Bob Hope, North Hollywood, California

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Bob_Hope_and_family.jpg/250px-Bob_Hope_and_family.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_and_family.jpg)

The Hope family; Back, from left: Tony, Dolores, and Linda; Front, from left: Kelly, Bob, and Nora

Hope was briefly married to vaudeville partner Grace Louise Troxell (1912–1992), a secretary from Chicago, Illinois. They were married on January 25, 1933, in Erie, Pennsylvania.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199866-128) They divorced in November 1934.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Sheridan_2014-129)

The couple had shared headliner status with Joe Howard at the Palace Theatre in April 1931, performing "Keep Smiling" and the "Antics of 1931".[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-130) They worked together at the RKO Albee, performing the "Antics of 1933" along with Ann Gillens and Johnny Peters in June of that year.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-131) The following month, singer [Dolores Reade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_Reade "Dolores Reade") joined Hope's vaudeville troupe and was performing with him at Loew's Metropolitan Theater. She was described as a "former [Ziegfeld beauty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziegfeld_girl "Ziegfeld girl") and one of society's favorite nightclub entertainers, having appeared at many private social functions at New York, Palm Beach, and Southampton".[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-132)

His marriage to Reade was fraught with ambiguities. As [Richard Zoglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Zoglin "Richard Zoglin") wrote in his 2014 biography _Hope: Entertainer of the Century_,

> Bob and Dolores always claimed that they married in February 1934 in Erie, Pennsylvania. But at that time, he was secretly married to his vaudeville partner Louise Troxell, after three years together on and off. I found divorce papers for Bob and Louise dated November 1934, so either Bob Hope was a bigamist, or he lied about marrying Dolores in February that year. He had actually married Louise in January 1933 in Erie when they were traveling on the vaudeville circuit. When he claimed he had married Dolores in Erie he was miles away in New York, on Broadway. More intriguing, there is no record anywhere of his marriage to Dolores, if it happened. And there are no wedding photos, either. But he never forgot Louise and quietly sent her money in her later years.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Sheridan_2014-129)

Dolores had been one of Hope's co-stars on Broadway in _Roberta_. The couple adopted four children: Linda (in 1939), Anthony "Tony" (1940–2004),[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-133) Kelly (1946), and Eleanora "Nora" (1946).[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199886%E2%80%9387-134) Bob and Dolores were also the legal guardians of Tracey, the youngest daughter of famous New York City bar owner [Bernard "Toots" Shor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toots_Shor "Toots Shor") and his wife, Marion "Baby" Shor.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-135) In 1935, the couple lived in Manhattan. In 1937, they moved to 10346 Moorpark Street in the [Toluca Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toluca_Lake "Toluca Lake") neighborhood of Los Angeles, where they would reside until their respective deaths.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-136)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-137)

Hope had a reputation as a womanizer and continued to see other women throughout his marriage.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk199882,_90-138) Zoglin wrote that Hope had several "affairs with chorus girls, beauty queens, singers and showbiz wannabes". Women who have claimed to have been romantically linked to Hope include [Barbara Payton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Payton "Barbara Payton"), [Marilyn Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marilyn_Maxwell "Marilyn Maxwell"), and [Rosemarie Frankland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemarie_Frankland "Rosemarie Frankland").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd200665-139)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd200666,_67-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd2006311-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd2006313-142)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEO'Dowd2006313-142)[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Arthur_Marx_1993-143)

### Politics and beliefs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Politics and beliefs")]

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg/250px-Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Campaign_event_in_California_-_NARA_-_194741.jpg)

From left to right: [Spiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiro_Agnew "Spiro Agnew") and [Judy Agnew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Agnew "Judy Agnew"), Bob and [Dolores Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_Hope "Dolores Hope"), [Richard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon") and [Pat Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Nixon "Pat Nixon"), [Nancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Reagan "Nancy Reagan") and [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan") during a campaign stop for the [Nixon-Agnew ticket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nixon-Agnew_ticket "Nixon-Agnew ticket") in California, 1971

Hope had extensive relationships with US Presidents from [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt") to [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") and often made topical political jokes in his comedic material. In an interview with Hope biographer [Richard Zoglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Zoglin "Richard Zoglin") on [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR") he stated that "Bob Hope was the establishment. After the shootings of president Ronald Reagan and [Pope John Paul II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_Paul_II "Pope John Paul II") in 1981, Hope advocated for [gun control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_control "Gun control"). Hope told [Tom Shales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Shales "Tom Shales") of _The Washington Post_, "I'm for gun registration. I don't think any jerk that's coked up or anything should be allowed to walk in a store and buy a gun and turn around and shoot 19 people, you know? ... Bush"), who was visiting [West Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Point "West Point") the same day Hope taped a special there, had declined to meet with him. Hope's views on the gay community also evolved. Most of us today are aware of Anita Bryant's stand [but] I still think jobs should be based on talent, not whether a person is homosexual or heterosexual."[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-153) However, Texaco and Chrysler, sponsors for many of his TV specials, asked him to refrain from making further jokes about the subject.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-154) In February 1986, he joined [Elizabeth Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Taylor "Elizabeth Taylor"), to cohost a benefit for [American Foundation for AIDS Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Foundation_for_AIDS_Research "American Foundation for AIDS Research") and the [Arizona AIDS Fund Trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_AIDS_Fund_Trust?action=edit&redlink=1 "Arizona AIDS Fund Trust (page does not exist)") in [Scottsdale, AZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scottsdale,_AZ "Scottsdale, AZ").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-155) Though expressing these supportive views, he occasionally used epithets and told jokes at the expense of the community yet showed remorse when called on it. During a performance at [Liberty Weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Weekend "Liberty Weekend") in 1986, Hope remarked, "I just heard that the [Statue of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty "Statue of Liberty") has AIDS, but she doesn't know if she got it from the mouth of the [Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River "Hudson River") or the [Staten Island Ferry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staten_Island_Ferry "Staten Island Ferry")."[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-156) Two months later, Hope took responsibility for telling the joke and apologized, explaining that he overheard the joke and thought it was funny.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-157) When Hope used the word "[fag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faggot "Faggot")" on a 1988 _[Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Tonight\_Show\_Starring\_Johnny\_Carson "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson")_ appearance, [GLAAD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GLAAD "GLAAD") asked for a statement apologizing for the slur. ### Philanthropy and estate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Philanthropy and estate")]

Hope, who suffered from vision problems for much of his adult life, served as an active honorary chairman on the board of [Fight for Sight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fight_for_Sight_(U.S.) "Fight for Sight (U.S.)"), a nonprofit organization in the United States which funds medical research in vision and ophthalmology. He hosted its _Lights On_ telecast in 1960 and donated $100,000 ($1.04M in 2024) to establish the Bob Hope Fight for Sight Fund.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Fight_for_Sight-159) Hope recruited numerous top celebrities for the annual "Lights On" fundraiser. As an example, he hosted boxing champion [Joe Frazier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Frazier "Joe Frazier"), actress [Yvonne De Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yvonne_De_Carlo "Yvonne De Carlo"), and singer-actor [Sergio Franchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Franchi "Sergio Franchi") as headliners for the April 25, 1971, show at Philharmonic Hall in [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee").[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Wilson_1971-160)

Hope settled into a home custom built for him in 1939 on an 87,000-square-foot (8,083 m 2) lot in the [Toluca Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toluca_Lake "Toluca Lake") section of [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California") in the [San Fernando Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Valley "San Fernando Valley"). It was put on the market in late 2012.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMikailian2012-161)

The [Hope Residence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hope_Residence "Hope Residence") is a 23,366-square-foot (2,171 m 2)[modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modernism "Modernism") home in [Palm Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Springs "Palm Springs"), built to resemble a volcano, that was designed in 1973 by [John Lautner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lautner "John Lautner"). The home is located above the city, with panoramic views of the [Coachella Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley "Coachella Valley") and the [San Jacinto Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jacinto_Mountains "San Jacinto Mountains"). It was put on the market for the first time in February 2013 with an asking price of $50 million,[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-NYTimes_February_2013-162) and sold to investor [Ron Burkle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Burkle "Ron Burkle") for just $13 million in November 2016.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-163)

### Advanced age and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bob_Hope&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Advanced age and death")]

At the age of 93, seven years before his death, Hope converted to [Catholicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholicism "Catholicism"), his wife's faith.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-seeing-stars_St_Charles-164)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-165)

In July 1997 at age 94, he attended the funeral of [James Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Stewart "James Stewart"), where many pointed out his frail appearance.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-166) At the age of 95, Hope made an appearance at the 50th anniversary of the [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") with [Milton Berle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Berle "Milton Berle") and [Sid Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sid_Caesar "Sid Caesar"). Contemporaries [Fay Wray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fay_Wray "Fay Wray") and [Gloria Stuart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloria_Stuart "Gloria Stuart") were also present.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Gallo_1998-167) Two years later, he was present at the opening of the Bob Hope Gallery of American Entertainment at the [Library of Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_of_Congress "Library of Congress"). The Library of Congress has presented two major exhibitions about Hope's life: "Hope for America: Performers, Politics and Pop Culture" and "Bob Hope and American Variety".[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-myloc_hopeforamerica-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-loc_bobhope-169) He last made an appearance at the Hope Classic in 2000, where he hugged Swedish golfer [Jesper Parnevik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesper_Parnevik "Jesper Parnevik").[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-170)

[![Image 32](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Bob_Hope_Grave.JPG/250px-Bob_Hope_Grave.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bob_Hope_Grave.JPG)

Graves of Bob and Dolores Hope, on the grounds of the Mission San Fernando Rey de España

In 1998, five years before his death, a prepared obituary written by [the Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Associated_Press "The Associated Press") was inadvertently released, resulting in Hope's death being announced on the floor of the [U.S. House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._House_of_Representatives "U.S. House of Representatives").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-c-span_June_1998-171)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEQuirk1998313-172) However, aside from increasing frailty, Hope remained in relatively good health until late in his old age.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGrudens2002148-173) In June 2000 at age 97, he spent nearly a week in a California hospital being treated for [gastrointestinal bleeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrointestinal_bleeding "Gastrointestinal bleeding").[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-CNN_June_2000-174) In August 2001 at age 98, he spent close to two weeks in a hospital recovering from [pneumonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumonia "Pneumonia").[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-175)[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-guardian_September_2001-176)

Hope celebrated his 100th birthday on May 29, 2003.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-USA_Today_May_2003-177) To mark this event, the intersection of [Hollywood and Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_and_Vine "Hollywood and Vine") in Los Angeles was named "Bob Hope Square" and his centennial was declared "Bob Hope Day" in 35 states. Even at 100, Hope maintained his self-deprecating sense of humor, quipping, "I'm so old, they've canceled my [blood type](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_type "Blood type")."[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-bbcdeath-178)

On July 27, 2003, Hope died of pneumonia at his home in [Toluca Lake, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toluca_Lake,_California "Toluca Lake, California").[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-bbcdeath-178) His grandson Zach Hope told [Soledad O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soledad_O'Brien "Soledad O'Brien") in an interview that, when asked at the end of his life where he wished to be buried, he said, "Surprise me".[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-CNN_July_29,_2003-179) His remains were temporarily placed in a mausoleum vault at the [San Fernando Mission Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Mission_Cemetery "San Fernando Mission Cemetery") before the construction of the Bob Hope Memorial Garden at the [San Fernando Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Mission "San Fernando Mission"), located next door to the cemetery, in Los Angeles. Dolores died in 2011, aged 102.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-180)[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-Doyle_2005-181) After his death, newspaper cartoonists worldwide paid tribute to his work for the USO, and some featured drawings of [Bing Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby"), who had died in 1977, welcoming Hope to Heaven.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope#cite_note-fac-assoc.org-182)

The **National Garden of American Heroes** is a proposed [sculpture garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sculpture_garden "Sculpture garden") honoring "great figures of America's history".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-order-1) The concept was first put forward by President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") in 2020 during an [Independence Day event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Rushmore_Fireworks_Celebration_2020 "Mount Rushmore Fireworks Celebration 2020") in [Keystone, South Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keystone,_South_Dakota "Keystone, South Dakota").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-gwinnett-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-NYT-AP-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Niedzwiadek-4) It was included in a series of [executive orders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_order "Executive order") issued by Trump in the final months of his first term in office that sought to address [conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States") cultural grievances.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Niedzwiadek-4) In July 2025, [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") passed the [One Big Beautiful Bill Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Big_Beautiful_Bill_Act "One Big Beautiful Bill Act"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-congress-5) which appropriates $40 million to establish and maintain the National Garden of American Heroes.

Trump's vision for the garden includes the creation of 250 statues depicting notable [Founding Fathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founding_Fathers_of_the_United_States "Founding Fathers of the United States"), activists, political figures, businesspeople, athletes, celebrities, and pop culture icons.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Niedzwiadek-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-6)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-NYT-AP-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-:0-9) Initial reactions from historians were largely negative, with many criticizing the choices as seemingly random and political.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10) Reactions by sculptors were also negative, with many describing the requested criteria for the statues as unrealistic and unworkable given the money and timetable expected.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Schaffer_05312025-11)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Trump's order said that the proposed garden would be managed by the Task Force for Building and Rebuilding Monuments to American Heroes, which would allocate funding from the [Interior Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Interior "United States Department of the Interior") to establish the site. Members of the task force would include chairs of the [National Endowment for the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Endowment_for_the_Arts "National Endowment for the Arts") and [National Endowment for the Humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Endowment_for_the_Humanities "National Endowment for the Humanities"), the [Administrator of General Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrator_of_General_Services "Administrator of General Services"), the chair of the [Advisory Council on Historic Preservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advisory_Council_on_Historic_Preservation "Advisory Council on Historic Preservation"), and any additional "officers or employees of any executive department or agency" designated by the president.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-hill-12) Trump described the garden as a response to the practice of [removing monuments and memorials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_monuments_and_memorials_removed_during_the_George_Floyd_protests "List of monuments and memorials removed during the George Floyd protests"); many such monuments were removed or destroyed in 2020 as part of a response to the [George Floyd protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-gwinnett-2)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-hill-12) In his Mount Rushmore speech announcing the proposal, Trump claimed that "Angry mobs are trying to tear down statues of our founders, deface our most sacred memorials and unleash a wave of violent crime in our cities" and pledged to build "a vast outdoor park that will feature the statues of the greatest Americans to ever live".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10)

Under Trump's Executive Order 13934, issued July 3, 2020, the task force was granted 60 days to develop preliminary plans for the site, including a potential location,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-13) and was to open before July 4, 2026, the [250th anniversary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Semiquincentennial "United States Semiquincentennial") of the adoption of the [Declaration of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-hill-12) The original executive order listed 31 historical figures as examples of those who would receive a statue in the Garden.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-order-1) On January 18, 2021—two days before leaving office—Trump signed a new executive order listing 244 historical figures, including all 31 previously named, of those who would receive statues.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-17) That revised list included 192 men and 52 women.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Alberti-18)

In 2021, the garden was considered highly unlikely to ever be built, and [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") never appropriated any funds for the project.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Sprunt-19) On May 14, 2021, President Joe Biden issued an executive order that revoked both of Trump's executive orders on the Garden, as well as various other Trump-issued executive orders.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Niedzwiadek-4)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Miller-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-21)

On January 29, 2025, Trump revoked Biden's executive order related to the garden and called for six additional names to be added to the list of historical figures. The timeline of its construction was modified from July 4, 2026, to "as expeditiously as possible".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-:0-9) During a 2025 [Black History Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_History_Month "Black History Month") reception at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House"), Trump said a statue of [Prince Estabrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Estabrook "Prince Estabrook"), a [Black Patriot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Patriot "Black Patriot"), would be in the garden.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-pe-22)[Vince Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Haley "Vince Haley"), chair of the [Domestic Policy Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Domestic_Policy_Council "United States Domestic Policy Council"), would be responsible for selecting the final list of 250 subjects.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-:1-23)

In March 2025 South Dakota Governor [Larry Rhoden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Rhoden "Larry Rhoden") sent Trump a proposal to build the garden in the [Black Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Hills "Black Hills") region in the state near [Mount Rushmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Rushmore "Mount Rushmore") on a plot of private land that will be donated.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-24)

In April 2025, the National Endowment for the Humanities announced it would sponsor grants to artists for the planned works, in a joint effort with the National Endowment for the Arts.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-:1-23)

On June 24, 2026, at a rally in the [National Mall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Mall "National Mall") to kick off the [Great American State Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_American_State_Fair "Great American State Fair"), Donald Trump announced the garden will be built in [West Potomac Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Potomac_Park "West Potomac Park").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-25)

### Funding and legislative authorization

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Funding and legislative authorization")]

In April 2025, the [National Endowment for the Humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Endowment_for_the_Humanities "National Endowment for the Humanities") announced a grant program of $200,000 per statue paid for in part by canceled grants for other arts and humanities projects by Elon Musk's [Department of Government Efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Government_Efficiency "Department of Government Efficiency"). It directed that statues were portrayed in a "realistic manner," with no modernist or abstract designs allowed.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-26) The Executive Order mandated further that the work must be "in the classical style, lifelike, and created from marble, granite, bronze, copper, or brass,".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-27)

In May 2025, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, a comprehensive budget reconciliation package.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-congress-5) Section 86001 of the bill appropriates $40 million to the Department of the Interior to establish and maintain the National Garden of American Heroes.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-28)

The bill's passage marked the first congressional funding for the garden, which had previously been authorized solely through executive orders during President Trump's first term.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-abs-29)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Initial reception by historians

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Initial reception by historians")]

In 2020, [James R. Grossman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Grossman "James Grossman"), the executive director of the [American Historical Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Historical_Association "American Historical Association"), said that "The choices vary from odd to probably inappropriate to provocative" and suggested that the proposal was an attempt by Trump "to seize on a cultural conflict to distract from other issues" during an election season, as suggested by the short (60-day) timetable that Trump set forth in his order.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10) Historian [Karen Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_L._Cox "Karen L. Cox") described the executive order about the proposed monument as "random" and said that "Nothing about this suggests it's thoughtful".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10) Historian Adam Domby noted that the initial proposal did not include [Native Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), although [Red Cloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cloud "Red Cloud"), [Chief Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Joseph "Chief Joseph"), [Sacagawea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacagawea "Sacagawea"), [Chief Sitting Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Sitting_Bull "Chief Sitting Bull"), [Tecumseh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tecumseh "Tecumseh"), and [Jim Thorpe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Thorpe "Jim Thorpe") have since been selected. Domby also noted that the initial proposal included General [George Patton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Patton "George Patton") but omitted President [Dwight D. Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower "Dwight D. Eisenhower"), although both generals were later slated for inclusion as are other historical military figures.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10) Several of the chosen statues were criticized for their stances on race, and criticism was made that the garden featured more conservative intellectuals than left-leaning ones.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Schaffer_05312025-11)

### Initial reception by sculptors

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Initial reception by sculptors")]

In 2025, _[Politico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politico "Politico")_ reported that sculptors who saw the design specifications for Trump's garden described it as unrealistic, and that "America doesn't have enough quality sculptors or museum-caliber foundries to make this happen on Trump's speedy timeline". Daniel Kunitz, editor of _[Sculpture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sculpture\_(magazine) "Sculpture (magazine)")_ magazine, called the proposal "completely unworkable". The report stated that most fine-arts foundries in the United States are booked six to 18 months in advance, and that sculpture experts mused the only place that could create the desired sculptures on the timetable requested was in China. It further quoted fine arts experts who stated that such collaborations ran the risk of having work be "slapdash and uninspired", and quoted one sculpture expert who likened the attempt to "a government-run version of [Madame Tussaud's wax museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame_Tussauds "Madame Tussauds")". The report questioned who would apply for the $200,000 commission, noting both low opinion of Trump in the artistic community and noting that the money offered was low after the costs of base casting and material were applied, which were requested to be granite, bronze, copper, or brass.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Schaffer_05312025-11)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Mount_Rushmore_Fireworks_Celebration_%2850082668053%29.jpg/250px-Mount_Rushmore_Fireworks_Celebration_%2850082668053%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mount_Rushmore_Fireworks_Celebration_(50082668053).jpg)

Trump announcing the garden proposal at the [Mount Rushmore Fireworks Celebration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Rushmore_Fireworks_Celebration_2020 "Mount Rushmore Fireworks Celebration 2020") on July 3, 2020

The **National Garden of American Heroes** is a proposed [sculpture garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sculpture_garden "Sculpture garden") honoring "great figures of America's history".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-order-1) The concept was first put forward by President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") in 2020 during an [Independence Day event](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Rushmore_Fireworks_Celebration_2020 "Mount Rushmore Fireworks Celebration 2020") in [Keystone, South Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keystone,_South_Dakota "Keystone, South Dakota").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-gwinnett-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-NYT-AP-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Niedzwiadek-4) It was included in a series of [executive orders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_order "Executive order") issued by Trump in the final months of his first term in office that sought to address [conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservatism_in_the_United_States "Conservatism in the United States") cultural grievances.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Niedzwiadek-4) In July 2025, [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") passed the [One Big Beautiful Bill Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Big_Beautiful_Bill_Act "One Big Beautiful Bill Act"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-congress-5) which appropriates $40 million to establish and maintain the National Garden of American Heroes.

Trump's vision for the garden includes the creation of 250 statues depicting notable [Founding Fathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founding_Fathers_of_the_United_States "Founding Fathers of the United States"), activists, political figures, businesspeople, athletes, celebrities, and pop culture icons.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Niedzwiadek-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-6)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-NYT-AP-3)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-:0-9) Initial reactions from historians were largely negative, with many criticizing the choices as seemingly random and political.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10) Reactions by sculptors were also negative, with many describing the requested criteria for the statues as unrealistic and unworkable given the money and timetable expected.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Schaffer_05312025-11)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Trump's order said that the proposed garden would be managed by the Task Force for Building and Rebuilding Monuments to American Heroes, which would allocate funding from the [Interior Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Interior "United States Department of the Interior") to establish the site. Members of the task force would include chairs of the [National Endowment for the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Endowment_for_the_Arts "National Endowment for the Arts") and [National Endowment for the Humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Endowment_for_the_Humanities "National Endowment for the Humanities"), the [Administrator of General Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrator_of_General_Services "Administrator of General Services"), the chair of the [Advisory Council on Historic Preservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advisory_Council_on_Historic_Preservation "Advisory Council on Historic Preservation"), and any additional "officers or employees of any executive department or agency" designated by the president.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-hill-12) Trump described the garden as a response to the practice of [removing monuments and memorials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_monuments_and_memorials_removed_during_the_George_Floyd_protests "List of monuments and memorials removed during the George Floyd protests"); many such monuments were removed or destroyed in 2020 as part of a response to the [George Floyd protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-gwinnett-2)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-hill-12) In his Mount Rushmore speech announcing the proposal, Trump claimed that "Angry mobs are trying to tear down statues of our founders, deface our most sacred memorials and unleash a wave of violent crime in our cities" and pledged to build "a vast outdoor park that will feature the statues of the greatest Americans to ever live".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10)

Under Trump's Executive Order 13934, issued July 3, 2020, the task force was granted 60 days to develop preliminary plans for the site, including a potential location,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-13) and was to open before July 4, 2026, the [250th anniversary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Semiquincentennial "United States Semiquincentennial") of the adoption of the [Declaration of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-hill-12) The original executive order listed 31 historical figures as examples of those who would receive a statue in the Garden.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-order-1) On January 18, 2021—two days before leaving office—Trump signed a new executive order listing 244 historical figures, including all 31 previously named, of those who would receive statues.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-17) That revised list included 192 men and 52 women.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Alberti-18)

In 2021, the garden was considered highly unlikely to ever be built, and [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") never appropriated any funds for the project.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Sprunt-19) On May 14, 2021, President Joe Biden issued an executive order that revoked both of Trump's executive orders on the Garden, as well as various other Trump-issued executive orders.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Niedzwiadek-4)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Miller-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-21)

On January 29, 2025, Trump revoked Biden's executive order related to the garden and called for six additional names to be added to the list of historical figures. The timeline of its construction was modified from July 4, 2026, to "as expeditiously as possible".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-:0-9) During a 2025 [Black History Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_History_Month "Black History Month") reception at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House"), Trump said a statue of [Prince Estabrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Estabrook "Prince Estabrook"), a [Black Patriot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Patriot "Black Patriot"), would be in the garden.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-pe-22)[Vince Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Haley "Vince Haley"), chair of the [Domestic Policy Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Domestic_Policy_Council "United States Domestic Policy Council"), would be responsible for selecting the final list of 250 subjects.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-:1-23)

In March 2025 South Dakota Governor [Larry Rhoden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Rhoden "Larry Rhoden") sent Trump a proposal to build the garden in the [Black Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Hills "Black Hills") region in the state near [Mount Rushmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Rushmore "Mount Rushmore") on a plot of private land that will be donated.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-24)

In April 2025, the National Endowment for the Humanities announced it would sponsor grants to artists for the planned works, in a joint effort with the National Endowment for the Arts.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-:1-23)

On June 24, 2026, at a rally in the [National Mall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Mall "National Mall") to kick off the [Great American State Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_American_State_Fair "Great American State Fair"), Donald Trump announced the garden will be built in [West Potomac Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Potomac_Park "West Potomac Park").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-25)

### Funding and legislative authorization

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Funding and legislative authorization")]

In April 2025, the [National Endowment for the Humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Endowment_for_the_Humanities "National Endowment for the Humanities") announced a grant program of $200,000 per statue paid for in part by canceled grants for other arts and humanities projects by Elon Musk's [Department of Government Efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Government_Efficiency "Department of Government Efficiency"). It directed that statues were portrayed in a "realistic manner," with no modernist or abstract designs allowed.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-26) The Executive Order mandated further that the work must be "in the classical style, lifelike, and created from marble, granite, bronze, copper, or brass,".[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-27)

In May 2025, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, a comprehensive budget reconciliation package.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-congress-5) Section 86001 of the bill appropriates $40 million to the Department of the Interior to establish and maintain the National Garden of American Heroes.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-28)

The bill's passage marked the first congressional funding for the garden, which had previously been authorized solely through executive orders during President Trump's first term.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-abs-29)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Initial reception by historians

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Initial reception by historians")]

In 2020, [James R. Grossman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Grossman "James Grossman"), the executive director of the [American Historical Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Historical_Association "American Historical Association"), said that "The choices vary from odd to probably inappropriate to provocative" and suggested that the proposal was an attempt by Trump "to seize on a cultural conflict to distract from other issues" during an election season, as suggested by the short (60-day) timetable that Trump set forth in his order.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10) Historian [Karen Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_L._Cox "Karen L. Cox") described the executive order about the proposed monument as "random" and said that "Nothing about this suggests it's thoughtful".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10) Historian Adam Domby noted that the initial proposal did not include [Native Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), although [Red Cloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Cloud "Red Cloud"), [Chief Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Joseph "Chief Joseph"), [Sacagawea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacagawea "Sacagawea"), [Chief Sitting Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Sitting_Bull "Chief Sitting Bull"), [Tecumseh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tecumseh "Tecumseh"), and [Jim Thorpe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Thorpe "Jim Thorpe") have since been selected. Domby also noted that the initial proposal included General [George Patton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Patton "George Patton") but omitted President [Dwight D. Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower "Dwight D. Eisenhower"), although both generals were later slated for inclusion as are other historical military figures.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-WanHistorian-10) Several of the chosen statues were criticized for their stances on race, and criticism was made that the garden featured more conservative intellectuals than left-leaning ones.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Schaffer_05312025-11)

### Initial reception by sculptors

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Garden_of_American_Heroes&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Initial reception by sculptors")]

In 2025, _[Politico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politico "Politico")_ reported that sculptors who saw the design specifications for Trump's garden described it as unrealistic, and that "America doesn't have enough quality sculptors or museum-caliber foundries to make this happen on Trump's speedy timeline". Daniel Kunitz, editor of _[Sculpture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sculpture\_(magazine) "Sculpture (magazine)")_ magazine, called the proposal "completely unworkable". The report stated that most fine-arts foundries in the United States are booked six to 18 months in advance, and that sculpture experts mused the only place that could create the desired sculptures on the timetable requested was in China. It further quoted fine arts experts who stated that such collaborations ran the risk of having work be "slapdash and uninspired", and quoted one sculpture expert who likened the attempt to "a government-run version of [Madame Tussaud's wax museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madame_Tussauds "Madame Tussauds")". The report questioned who would apply for the $200,000 commission, noting both low opinion of Trump in the artistic community and noting that the money offered was low after the costs of base casting and material were applied, which were requested to be granite, bronze, copper, or brass.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Bob_Hope#cite_note-Schaffer_05312025-11)

An **off-by-one error** or **off-by-one bug** (known by acronyms **OBOE**, **OBOB**, **OBO**, and **OB1**) is a [logic error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic_error "Logic error") that involves a number that differs from its intended value by 1. An off-by-one error can sometimes appear in a [mathematical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics") context. It also often occurs in [computer programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming "Computer programming") when a [loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Control_flow#Loops "Control flow") iterates one time too many or too few, usually caused by the use of non-strict inequality (≤) as the terminating condition where strict inequality (<) should have been used, or vice versa. Off-by-one errors also stem from confusion over [zero-based numbering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-based_numbering "Zero-based numbering").

## Cases

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Off-by-one_error&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Cases")]

### Fencepost error

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Off-by-one_error&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Fencepost error")]

A **fencepost error** (occasionally called a **telegraph pole**, **lamp-post**, or **picket fence error**) is a specific type of off-by-one error. An early description of this error appears in the works of [Vitruvius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitruvius "Vitruvius").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OB1#cite_note-1) The following problem illustrates the error:

> If you build a straight [fence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fence "Fence") 30 feet long with posts spaced 3 feet apart, how many posts do you need?

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Fencepost_error_01.svg/330px-Fencepost_error_01.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fencepost_error_01.svg)

A straight fence with 10 sections requires 11 posts. More generally, _n_ sections would require _n_ + 1 posts.

The common answer of 10 posts is wrong. This response comes from dividing the length of the fence by the spacing apart from each post, with the quotient being erroneously classified as the number of posts. In actuality, the fence has 10 sections and 11 posts.

In this scenario, a fence with _n_ sections will have _n_ + 1 posts. Conversely, if the fence contains _n_ posts, it will contain _n_ − 1 sections. This relationship is important to consider when dealing with the reverse error. The reverse error occurs when the number of posts is known and the number of sections is assumed to be the same. Depending on the design of the fence, this assumption can be correct or incorrect.

The following problem demonstrates the reverse error:

> If you have _n_ posts, how many sections are there between them?

The interpretation for the fence's design changes the answer to this problem. The correct number of sections for a fence is _n_ − 1 if the fence is a free-standing line segment bounded by a post at each of its ends (e.g., a fence between two passageway gaps), _n_ if the fence forms one complete, free-standing loop (e.g., enclosure accessible by surmounting, such as a boxing ring), or _n_ + 1 if posts do not occur at the ends of a line-segment-like fence (e.g., a fence between and wall-anchored to two buildings). The precise problem definition must be carefully considered, as the setup for one situation may give the wrong answer for other situations.

Fencepost errors can also occur in units other than length. For example, the [Time Pyramid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Pyramid "Time Pyramid"), consisting of 120 blocks placed at 10-year intervals between blocks, is scheduled to take 1,190 years to build (not 1,200), from the installation of the first block to the last block. One of the earliest fencepost errors involved time, where the [Julian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_calendar "Julian calendar") originally [calculated leap years incorrectly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_calendar#Leap_year_error "Julian calendar"), due to counting inclusively rather than exclusively, yielding a leap year every three years rather than every four.

An example of this error can occur in the computational language [MATLAB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MATLAB "MATLAB") with the `linspace()`[linear interpolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_interpolation "Linear interpolation") function, whose parameters are `(lower value, upper value, number of values)` and not `(lower value, upper value, number of increments)`. A programmer who misunderstands the third parameter to be the number of increments might hope that `linspace(0,10,5)` would achieve a sequence `[0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10]` but instead would get `[0, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10]`.

### Looping over arrays

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Off-by-one_error&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Looping over arrays")]

Consider an [array](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Array_data_type "Array data type") of items, and items _m_ through _n_ (inclusive) are to be processed. How many items are there? An intuitive answer may be _n_ − _m_, but that is off by one, exhibiting a fencepost error; the correct answer is _n_ − _m_ + 1. For this reason, ranges in computing are often represented by [half-open intervals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-open_interval "Half-open interval"); the range from _m_ to _n_ (inclusive) is represented by the range from _m_ (inclusive) to _n_ + 1 (exclusive) to avoid fencepost errors. For example, a [loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Program_loop "Program loop") that iterates five times (from 0 to 4 inclusive) can be written as a half-open interval from 0 to 5:

for (index = 0; index < 5; index++) 
{
 /* Body of the loop */
}

The loop body is executed first of all with index equal to 0; index then becomes 1, 2, 3, and finally 4 on successive iterations. At that point, index becomes 5, so index < 5 is false and the loop ends. However, if the comparison used were <= (less than or equal to), the loop would be carried out six times: index takes the values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Likewise, if index were initialized to 1 rather than 0, there would only be four iterations: index takes the values 1, 2, 3, and 4. Both of these alternatives can cause off-by-one errors.

Another such error can occur if a [do-while loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do-while_loop "Do-while loop") is used in place of a [while loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/While_loop "While loop") (or vice versa). A do-while loop is guaranteed to run at least once.

Array-related confusion may also result from differences in programming languages. Numbering from 0 is most common, but some languages start array numbering with 1. [Pascal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pascal_(programming_language) "Pascal (programming language)") has arrays with user-defined indices. This makes it possible to model the array indices after the problem domain.

### Security implications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Off-by-one_error&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Security implications")]

A common off-by-one error which results in a security-related bug is caused by misuse of the [C standard library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_standard_library "C standard library")`strncat` routine. A common misconception with `strncat` is that the guaranteed null termination will not write beyond the maximum length. In reality, it will write a terminating null character one byte beyond the maximum length specified. The following code contains such a bug:

void foo (char *s) 
{
 char buf[15];
 memset(buf, 0, sizeof(buf));
 strncat(buf, s, sizeof(buf)); // Final parameter should be: sizeof(buf)-1
}

Off-by-one errors can occur when using the C library because it is not consistent with respect to whether one needs to subtract 1 byte; functions like `fgets()` and `strncpy` will never write past the length given to them (`fgets()` subtracts 1 itself, and only retrieves [_n_ − 1] bytes), whereas others, like `strncat`, will write past the length given to them. On some systems ([little endian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endianness "Endianness") architectures in particular) this behavior can result in the overwriting of the least significant byte of the [frame pointer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frame_pointer "Frame pointer"). This can cause an exploitable condition where an attacker can hijack the local variables for the calling routine.

One approach that often helps avoid such problems is to use variants of these functions that calculate how much to write based on the total length of the buffer, rather than the maximum number of characters to write. Such functions include `strlcat` and `strlcpy`, and are often considered "safer" because they make it easier to avoid accidentally writing past the end of a buffer. (In the code example above, calling `strlcat(buf, s, sizeof(buf))` instead would remove the bug.)

An **off-by-one error** or **off-by-one bug** (known by acronyms **OBOE**, **OBOB**, **OBO**, and **OB1**) is a [logic error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic_error "Logic error") that involves a number that differs from its intended value by 1. An off-by-one error can sometimes appear in a [mathematical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics") context. It also often occurs in [computer programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming "Computer programming") when a [loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Control_flow#Loops "Control flow") iterates one time too many or too few, usually caused by the use of non-strict inequality (≤) as the terminating condition where strict inequality (<) should have been used, or vice versa. Off-by-one errors also stem from confusion over [zero-based numbering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-based_numbering "Zero-based numbering").

## Cases

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Off-by-one_error&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Cases")]

### Fencepost error

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Off-by-one_error&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Fencepost error")]

A **fencepost error** (occasionally called a **telegraph pole**, **lamp-post**, or **picket fence error**) is a specific type of off-by-one error. An early description of this error appears in the works of [Vitruvius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitruvius "Vitruvius").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OB1#cite_note-1) The following problem illustrates the error:

> If you build a straight [fence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fence "Fence") 30 feet long with posts spaced 3 feet apart, how many posts do you need?

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/Fencepost_error_01.svg/330px-Fencepost_error_01.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fencepost_error_01.svg)

A straight fence with 10 sections requires 11 posts. More generally, _n_ sections would require _n_ + 1 posts.

The common answer of 10 posts is wrong. This response comes from dividing the length of the fence by the spacing apart from each post, with the quotient being erroneously classified as the number of posts. In actuality, the fence has 10 sections and 11 posts.

In this scenario, a fence with _n_ sections will have _n_ + 1 posts. Conversely, if the fence contains _n_ posts, it will contain _n_ − 1 sections. This relationship is important to consider when dealing with the reverse error. The reverse error occurs when the number of posts is known and the number of sections is assumed to be the same. Depending on the design of the fence, this assumption can be correct or incorrect.

The following problem demonstrates the reverse error:

> If you have _n_ posts, how many sections are there between them?

The interpretation for the fence's design changes the answer to this problem. The correct number of sections for a fence is _n_ − 1 if the fence is a free-standing line segment bounded by a post at each of its ends (e.g., a fence between two passageway gaps), _n_ if the fence forms one complete, free-standing loop (e.g., enclosure accessible by surmounting, such as a boxing ring), or _n_ + 1 if posts do not occur at the ends of a line-segment-like fence (e.g., a fence between and wall-anchored to two buildings). The precise problem definition must be carefully considered, as the setup for one situation may give the wrong answer for other situations.

Fencepost errors can also occur in units other than length. For example, the [Time Pyramid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Pyramid "Time Pyramid"), consisting of 120 blocks placed at 10-year intervals between blocks, is scheduled to take 1,190 years to build (not 1,200), from the installation of the first block to the last block. One of the earliest fencepost errors involved time, where the [Julian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_calendar "Julian calendar") originally [calculated leap years incorrectly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_calendar#Leap_year_error "Julian calendar"), due to counting inclusively rather than exclusively, yielding a leap year every three years rather than every four.

An example of this error can occur in the computational language [MATLAB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MATLAB "MATLAB") with the `linspace()`[linear interpolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_interpolation "Linear interpolation") function, whose parameters are `(lower value, upper value, number of values)` and not `(lower value, upper value, number of increments)`. A programmer who misunderstands the third parameter to be the number of increments might hope that `linspace(0,10,5)` would achieve a sequence `[0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10]` but instead would get `[0, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10]`.

### Looping over arrays

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Off-by-one_error&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Looping over arrays")]

Consider an [array](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Array_data_type "Array data type") of items, and items _m_ through _n_ (inclusive) are to be processed. How many items are there? An intuitive answer may be _n_ − _m_, but that is off by one, exhibiting a fencepost error; the correct answer is _n_ − _m_ + 1. For this reason, ranges in computing are often represented by [half-open intervals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Half-open_interval "Half-open interval"); the range from _m_ to _n_ (inclusive) is represented by the range from _m_ (inclusive) to _n_ + 1 (exclusive) to avoid fencepost errors. For example, a [loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Program_loop "Program loop") that iterates five times (from 0 to 4 inclusive) can be written as a half-open interval from 0 to 5:

for (index = 0; index < 5; index++) 
{
 /* Body of the loop */
}

The loop body is executed first of all with index equal to 0; index then becomes 1, 2, 3, and finally 4 on successive iterations. At that point, index becomes 5, so index < 5 is false and the loop ends. However, if the comparison used were <= (less than or equal to), the loop would be carried out six times: index takes the values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Likewise, if index were initialized to 1 rather than 0, there would only be four iterations: index takes the values 1, 2, 3, and 4. Both of these alternatives can cause off-by-one errors.

Another such error can occur if a [do-while loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do-while_loop "Do-while loop") is used in place of a [while loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/While_loop "While loop") (or vice versa). A do-while loop is guaranteed to run at least once.

Array-related confusion may also result from differences in programming languages. Numbering from 0 is most common, but some languages start array numbering with 1. [Pascal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pascal_(programming_language) "Pascal (programming language)") has arrays with user-defined indices. This makes it possible to model the array indices after the problem domain.

### Security implications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Off-by-one_error&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Security implications")]

A common off-by-one error which results in a security-related bug is caused by misuse of the [C standard library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_standard_library "C standard library")`strncat` routine. A common misconception with `strncat` is that the guaranteed null termination will not write beyond the maximum length. In reality, it will write a terminating null character one byte beyond the maximum length specified. The following code contains such a bug:

void foo (char *s) 
{
 char buf[15];
 memset(buf, 0, sizeof(buf));
 strncat(buf, s, sizeof(buf)); // Final parameter should be: sizeof(buf)-1
}

Off-by-one errors can occur when using the C library because it is not consistent with respect to whether one needs to subtract 1 byte; functions like `fgets()` and `strncpy` will never write past the length given to them (`fgets()` subtracts 1 itself, and only retrieves [_n_ − 1] bytes), whereas others, like `strncat`, will write past the length given to them. On some systems ([little endian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endianness "Endianness") architectures in particular) this behavior can result in the overwriting of the least significant byte of the [frame pointer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frame_pointer "Frame pointer"). This can cause an exploitable condition where an attacker can hijack the local variables for the calling routine.

One approach that often helps avoid such problems is to use variants of these functions that calculate how much to write based on the total length of the buffer, rather than the maximum number of characters to write. Such functions include `strlcat` and `strlcpy`, and are often considered "safer" because they make it easier to avoid accidentally writing past the end of a buffer. (In the code example above, calling `strlcat(buf, s, sizeof(buf))` instead would remove the bug.)
